summary: Source-anchored research for Google Workspace SAML Federation. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: Configure a custom SAML app in Google Admin. Exchange Google SSO URL, Entity ID and signing certificate for Atlas ACS URL and Audience URI; Atlas supplies the Start/Login URL. (high confidence)
Enable the SAML app for everyone or selected organizational units/access groups, and test the login flow. App assignment is a separate setup step from creating the SAML metadata. (high confidence)
Enable Signed Response for the Atlas custom app. Google otherwise signs only the assertion by default, while the MongoDB setup explicitly requires a signed response. (high confidence)

Google documents a maximum of 75 groups in a custom SAML app group-membership mapping. This is a Google app configuration limit, not evidence of an Atlas-wide group limit. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-22)

StrongDM describes its G Suite SSO–MongoDB Atlas connection as a custom StrongDM integration for unified access. Its page is evidence for an intermediary access product, rather than instructions for configuring native Atlas SAML federation. (low confidence)

Google Workspace can act as the SAML identity provider for Atlas UI access, letting assigned users sign in with corporate credentials; this configuration does not itself establish database authentication. (high confidence)

MongoDB specifies HTTP POST request binding, SHA-256 response signature algorithm, Signed Response enabled, Name ID format UNSPECIFIED and Primary Email as Name ID for the Workspace integration. (low confidence)

Map Google first and last name fields to case-sensitive firstName and lastName. A Workspace user reported that missing these mappings caused new-user SSO failures at okta/hooks/acserror even while existing users could log in. (medium confidence)

Optional Atlas role mapping uses a single Google group-membership mapping row containing all selected groups and the app attribute memberOf. Google includes only the selected groups to which the user belongs, directly or indirectly. (high confidence)

Verify and associate an email domain in Atlas to route matching sign-ins to Google Workspace. If multiple SAML identity providers share that domain, MongoDB says the cloud console routes to the first configured one; use a specific SP- or IdP-initiated URL for an alternative. (low confidence)
Before testing domain routing, MongoDB recommends saving the Bypass SAML Mode URL, retaining the Federation Management Console session, and testing in a private browser window. (low confidence)

MongoDB documents Google Workspace as a SAML identity provider for signing in to Atlas and other MongoDB cloud services; Google supports custom SAML applications using managed Google Account credentials. (high confidence)
MongoDB specifies HTTP POST binding and SHA-256, Name ID format UNSPECIFIED with Primary Email, and case-sensitive firstName and lastName attribute mappings. (low confidence)

Users need the Google SAML application enabled for them. Google supports enabling access for everyone, organizational units or access groups; its guide also requires matching sign-in email addresses. (high confidence)

Apono advertises Google Workspace-driven granular permissions and access-request workflows as capabilities of connecting Apono with Google Workspace. That page does not establish equivalent native Atlas SAML database-permission automation. (low confidence)

Google requires a super administrator for the documented custom SAML app setup. MongoDB separately requires Atlas Organization Owner access and describes the Google prerequisite more broadly as administrative privileges. (medium confidence)
